metric_definitions.unrouted, clearance_violations, vias: the result manifest's board_statistics (connections.incomplete_count, clearance_violations.total_count, vias.total_count): Freerouting's board model on the routed board; n06_run.py copies them into summary.json as `statistics`
metric_definitions.session_differences: 1 if the arm's SES differs byte for byte from the baseline arm's on that board
metric_definitions.ripup_random_pass_connections: run_stats counter (--stats json, total.counts), in either arm: batch connections routed with ripup allowed in a pass whose number draws the random factor (4, 5, 7, 8, ...)
metric_definitions.ripup_random_factor_draws: run_stats counter: ripup cost evaluations that drew the random factor; 0 under Java's behaviour
metric_definitions.any_angle_skip_length_flips: run_stats counter, in either arm: any-angle end smoothings whose short-segment skip the switch's other value decides differently
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected, drc_real, via_in_pad,: the canary-pwr plugin row's grade (canary hardware/tools/grade.sh)

accept: Reachability first: a row whose baseline ripup_random_pass_connections is 0 never reaches a pass that draws; its ripup_pass_no_unset session must equal the baseline's. If every row reads 0, the switch is not measured by this set and stays true (N06.12 records it).

Verdict pair (baseline, ripup_pass_no_unset), the totals rule with accept=improve: no new clearance violation on any DSN row, the plugin row's via_in_pad and below_minimum 0 and drc_real no higher than baseline's; the candidate's unrouted summed over the DSN rows plus the plugin row's kicad_unconnected lower than the baseline's by more than the set's noise, sqrt of the sum of the bands squared (sqrt(8*2^2 + 10^2) = 11.49); no row worse by more than twice its band. Otherwise ripup_pass_no_unset stays true in both profiles, with these numbers.

Reported pair (baseline, any_angle_skip_length_squared): if any_angle_skip_length_flips is 0 in every run and every session equals its baseline, the fix is accepted on its test (any_angle::tests::skip_length_switch_both_behaviours_and_counter); otherwise the totals rule's no-regress form over the three any-angle rows (noise sqrt(3*2^2) = 3.46), with no new clearance violation. Its 45-degree rows and the plugin row cannot differ (the any-angle tightener does not run there); a difference on one is a bug to report.
stop_rule: One run per arm per row. No heavy run by the implementer.

orchestrator: Run orchestrator_command from the worktree root: it runs each arms.command on each boards.files row (8 rows x 3 arms = 24 runs), checks the input hashes, compares each SES with the baseline's and writes summary.json (session_differences, counts, statistics). plugin_canary.source: CANary hardware/canary-pwr-rev1.0, the original KiCad project at canary 9511d9a (git archive, unedited), as in N06.10's plugin-path run; never edit the source project.
plugin_canary.route: For each registered arm, run the release CLI on the plugin-exported DSN with the generated <stem>.args.json args verbatim, then append --router.profile=legacy, the arm's two explicit --router.java_quirks.* flags, --stats json --stats-out <arm>/stats.json and --result-json=<arm>/result.json. One exported input and one argument list serve every arm. Compare each session with the plugin baseline arm's.

Retain export/import logs, versions, source hashes and grades.

amendments.reason: main moved on before any N06.12 route (N06.14, N06.15, Q10.4, the measuring fixes 4885a30, 019b260 and 8f302b2, and the N06.3 audit d9d2dc3 were committed after 81afaba); freerouting-dev gate --prereg (4d44676) can judge the registered pairs, but not this registration's records as written (the DSN rows have no hard metric, so they would be UNGRADED, and canary-pwr-plugin is not in boards.files, so the run would be REFUSED); and the hard guards were checked against the baseline arm before any number. Written before any route of N06.12
amendments.changes: (1) engine base moved from main bbd1336 with N06.12's diff to main ceeebdf (N06.12's diff committed as 81afaba). Every java_quirks switch added since (N06.14, N06.15) defaults to true (Java), ENHANCED is unchanged, and the arms run under legacy with both keys explicit, so the arms still differ only in the two keys; the commands call the absolute binary they name, built at ceeebdf. (2) Plugin row hard guards: its baseline arm's configuration (legacy, the exported args, every java_quirks key true) is the one N06.7, N06.5 and N06.6 graded (session 986e30bd: 0 via-in-pad, 0 track_width), so the plugin row's baseline breaks no hard guard by that number. (3) The plugin row joins the gate: boards.files gains canary-pwr-plugin, hashed as the plugin-exported DSN its arms route (export of canary 9511d9a, unedited, with canary-graded-flow.json by kicad-plugin at main ceeebdf on WSL KiCad 10.0.7, made before any route; the body equals the export N06.5 and N06.6 routed (65ef16a8), only the first line, the DSN's own path, differs, and the args are the same), and boards.outside_runner lists it, so n06_run.py skips it and the plugin_canary procedure routes it as registered. Its record carries kicad_unconnected and drc_real from the grade and unrouted null (the router's own count is reported as plugin_unrouted), so its signal is kicad_unconnected, as the accept text says; its clearance_violations is null (the accept text guards clearance on the DSN rows only; the router's count is reported). (4) Hard metrics on every row, so that none is null for freerouting-dev gate --prereg: on a DSN row via_in_pad and below_minimum are N06.4 amendment 2's, counted on the routed board with the input's session wiring stripped (main 019b260), the session read at the writer's scale (main 8f302b2), by a tool on the engine API: vias in an SMD pad that the input has no via for (main 4885a30's added_via_in_pad), and delivered traces narrower than the board's narrowest class width that the input does not already have; on the plugin row via_in_pad is via_in_pad.py's count and below_minimum KiCad's track_width error count. On every row both are option (b), no new breach versus baseline: the arm's count minus the baseline arm's on the same row, floored at 0, with the raw counts reported as via_in_pad_raw and below_minimum_raw; the accept text's 'the plugin row's via_in_pad and below_minimum 0' reads as this option (b) count. (5) Hard-guard check before any number: the router's pin neck-down (a trace entering a pad narrower than its width is drawn at the pad's width, profile legacy included) puts copper under the narrowest class width on Java's baseline (N06.5's legacy sessions had 37 such traces on Issue026-J2_reference, 11 on bm08 and 1 on J2's 90 degree variant), and this set routes J2 and rpi_splitter in their any-angle variants, whose counts under the baseline arm are not known before this run, so a DSN row's below_minimum can be broken by the baseline arm under an absolute limit; option (b) keeps that breach from deciding the verdict. Where the baseline arm's count is 0, option (b) is the absolute limit. (6) The verdict pair (baseline, ripup_pass_no_unset) is computed by freerouting-dev gate --prereg with --arms baseline,ripup_pass_no_unset (accept improve, as registered) on records built from n06_run.py's summary.json and the plugin row, after the reachability clause is read from the counters and session hashes. The reported pair (baseline, any_angle_skip_length_squared) is judged as its accept clause says: reachability from any_angle_skip_length_flips and the session hashes first; if reached, its no-regress form over the three any-angle rows (noise sqrt(3*2^2) = 3.46) is computed by freerouting-dev gate --rule totals --accept no-regress with those three rows' bands on the records of those rows, because gate --prereg applies the registration's accept=improve to every pair; gate --prereg --all-pairs is run as well and its output for that pair is reported only. The arms, their commands and settings, the DSN rows, the metrics, the rule, the noise bands and the accept text's arithmetic are unchanged. (7) seen_before_registration is added (it was missing) and says what was seen at registration and before this amendment.
